rows.quote: Fenland, a proteome-wide proteome association study of 10,708 participants of European ancestry, used the SomaScan v4 assay with 4979 single-stranded oligonucleotides (aptamers) targeting 4775 unique proteins [13].
rows.reference_quote: Pietzner M, Wheeler E, Carrasco-Zanini J, Cortes A, Koprulu M, Wörheide MA et al. Mapping the proteo-genomic convergence of human diseases. Sci (New York NY).374(6569):eabj1541.
rows.coder_note: The sentence attributes the Fenland data to reference 13 (DOI 10.1126/science.abj1541), the source of the Pietzner 2021 row only; it also gives 10,708 participants, SomaScan v4, 4979 aptamers and 4775 proteins, which are that row's; no conflict elsewhere in the passages.

rows.quote: Using the SomaScan Multiple Aptamer Assay (version 4) in 35,559 Icelandic individuals with genotypic and phenotypic data, the deCODE study measured plasma protein levels [12], including 4,907 aptamers and 4,719 proteins.
rows.reference_quote: Ferkingstad E, Sulem P, Atlason BA, Sveinbjornsson G, Magnusson MI, Styrmisdottir EL, et al. Large-scale integration of the plasma proteome with genetics and disease. Nat Genet. 2021;53(12):1712–21.
rows.coder_note: The sentence attributes the deCODE data to reference 12 (DOI 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w), the source of the Ferkingstad 2021 row only, and gives 35,559 Icelandic individuals on SomaScan version 4 with 4,907 aptamers, that row's exact N and platform; not the Eldjarn 2023 row's 35,892.
